claim_as_stated: CEQ's NEPA regulations were removed (interim final rule 2025; final removal effective Jan 8, 2026?) and agencies adopted their own procedures (DOI handbook; USDA 7 CFR 1b).
stated_by: statecraft (PI-NEPA-02, PI-NEPA-04, PI-NEPA-05; SC-009, SC-011, SC-014)
correct_statement: CEQ's interim final rule (90 FR 10610, Feb 25, 2025; effective Apr 11, 2025) removed 40 CFR parts 1500-1508; CEQ adopted it as final without change at 91 FR 618 (Jan 8, 2026), effective Jan 8, 2026. CEQ reasons it may lack authority to issue binding rules after EO 14154 revoked EO 11991. Agencies follow their own procedures (CEQ guidance/template 90 FR 47734, Oct 2, 2025). DOI final rule 91 FR 8738 (Feb 24, 2026; effective same day) keeps a slimmed 43 CFR part 46 and moves most procedures to the 'Department of the Interior Handbook: National Environmental Policy Act Implementing Procedures'. USDA final rule (published and effective Apr 3, 2026) consolidates USDA procedures in 7 CFR part 1b and rescinds 36 CFR part 220 (Forest Service) in full; applies to CEs immediately, EAs published after May 18, 2026 and EISs with NOI after Jul 2, 2026.
source_title: Removal of National Environmental Policy Act Implementing Regulations (final rule); National Environmental Policy Act Implementing Regulations (DOI final rule); National Environmental Policy Act (USDA final rule, FR Doc 2026-06537)
source_publisher: Council on Environmental Quality (Federal Register); Department of the Interior (Federal Register); USDA (Federal Register public inspection); WilmerHale client alert
note: Drop the question mark: Jan 8, 2026 effective date confirmed. Do not call the DOI handbook '516 DM 1' (the final rule names it the DOI NEPA Handbook; 516 DM is cited only as where pre-2008 procedures lived). USDA FR page: statecraft cites 91 FR 17092, WilmerHale cites 91 FR 17,062; page not confirmed from primary - cite by date and FR Doc 2026-06537 until checked.

claim_as_stated: Seven County Infrastructure Coalition v. Eagle County (May 2025) - 'substantial deference' to agency NEPA judgments.
correct_statement: Seven County Infrastructure Coalition v. Eagle County, No. 23-975, decided May 29, 2025: Kavanaugh for the Court (Roberts, Thomas, Alito, Barrett); Sotomayor concurred in the judgment (Kagan, Jackson); Gorsuch did not participate. The D.C. Circuit 'failed to afford the Board the substantial judicial deference required in NEPA cases'; agencies need not analyze effects of separate upstream/downstream projects; 'NEPA requires agencies to focus on the environmental effects of the project at issue.'
source_title: Seven County Infrastructure Coalition v. Eagle County (opinion text)
source_publisher: Supreme Court of the United States (via Cornell LII)
note: Statecraft's '(5-3)' is misleading: judgment was 8-0 (reversed and remanded); the majority opinion had 5 votes and 3 concurred in the judgment. Say '8-0 judgment; 5-justice majority opinion'. U.S. Reports cite 605 U.S. 168 not shown on fetched page.

claim_as_stated: SPEED Act passed the House (Dec 18, 2025); current Senate status; key provisions (150-day limitations period; standing tied to substantive comments).
correct_statement: H.R. 4776 (SPEED Act, Rep. Westerman) passed the House 221-196 on Dec 18, 2025 (Roll Call 356); same day received in the Senate and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works. No later Senate action is recorded (latest action Dec 18, 2025); not enacted. As passed: claims generally barred unless filed within 150 days of publication of final agency action; where a comment period occurred, only parties that submitted a 'substantive and unique comment' may sue; remand is the sole remedy, with the action left in effect during a 180-day cure period; 'substantial deference' codified; effects limited to those with a 'reasonably close causal relationship' to the project.
source_title: H.R. 4776 timeline (congressional record data); SPEED Act Passes House (Law and the Environment blog)
source_publisher: The Lobby News (Congress.gov data mirror); Foley Hoag LLP
note: Status taken from a Congress.gov data mirror; re-check congress.gov immediately before publication. Separate Senate bill S. 3224 (statecraft) not checked. Describe as 'passed House; pending in Senate EPW', not as law.

claim_as_stated: NEPA s.112 sponsor-funded expedited reviews (180-day EA / 1-year EIS) - status and use.
correct_statement: NEPA section 112, added by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (Pub. L. 119-21, signed Jul 4, 2025), lets a project sponsor pay a fee of 125% of the anticipated cost of preparing or supervising the document in exchange for deadlines of 180 days for an EA (from fee payment) and 1 year for an EIS (from the NOI). Sponsors submit a project description and a declaration on whether they will prepare the document under NEPA s.107(f) to CEQ, which must set the fee within 15 days. The provision is in force; CEQ maintains an intake page on nepa.gov.
source_title: Section 112 NEPA Project Sponsor Opt-In Fees; The One Big Beautiful Bill Act Offers Expedited NEPA Review for a Fee
source_publisher: Council on Environmental Quality (nepa.gov); O'Melveny & Myers
note: Use: no public count or list of projects using s.112 found (not-found for the 'use' half). The CEQ page does not state the 125% figure; it comes from the statute as summarized by counsel. The claim that s.112 does not speed ESA/NHPA reviews is a reasonable reading (the section covers only NEPA documents) but was not confirmed in a source this pass.
